propositions: The pytest (macos-latest, py3.13) job is the critical path bottleneck at 18.6m, with --cov collection consuming 15.4m of that duration while macOS coverage output is never consumed.
macOS runner concurrency is scarce (peak 4 concurrent observed), so a slower macOS job holds other changes queued for 6.7-8.4m, turning a 21m run into 41-47m wall-clock time.

Coverage collection is redundantly enforced on three ubuntu cells running the identical test selection (7856 tests) with the same fail_under=70 floor, making macOS coverage collection pure duplicate work.
The default-suite step must conditionally omit --cov flags on macOS while preserving them on ubuntu, without altering the test selection or execution parameters on either platform.
GitHub Actions workflow_dispatch resolves reusable workflows from the default branch at submission time, not from the patchset, so workflow changes cannot be measured on their own Verified run.
